title: Saturation must be judged against the sensor's real ADU ceiling, not a hardcoded 65024
cause: Both image validators compared pixels against a fixed 16-bit constant (65024). The constant is correct only for a sensor whose driver LEFT-justifies sub-16-bit samples into the u16 container. A driver that right-justifies (INDI CCDs and several ASCOM drivers deliver a 12-bit sensor as 0..4095) clips at 4095, which never reaches 65024, so a fully clipped frame fell through to the uniform-frame check and was reported as 'possible sensor failure or dead frame'. CameraStatus.max_adu / SensorInfo.max_adu, which already carry the container full scale, were never consulted by the imaging crate.

findings.claim: The gap is real but NOT the one stated verbatim: on LEFT-justified 12-/14-bit sensors 65024 does fire
findings.evidence: imaging/src/fits.rs pre-existing tests test_comprehensive_12bit_saturation_detected (65520) and test_comprehensive_real_asi1600_saturation_not_dead_frame (65504) passed before this change. A left-justified 12-bit sensor tops out at 4095<<4 = 65520 > 65024.
findings.consequence: The failing population is right-justified sub-16-bit delivery (0..4095 / 0..16383), not '12-/14-bit sensors' as a class. Fix scoped accordingly.

findings.claim: Severing the wiring reproduces the exact field misdiagnosis
findings.evidence: With the ceiling resolution reverted, test_right_justified_12bit_clip_is_saturation_not_a_dead_sensor fails with: expected a saturation error at the 12-bit ceiling, got ["All 65536 pixels have identical value 4095 - possible sensor failure or dead frame"]
findings.consequence: An over-exposed user was being told their camera was broken.

findings.claim: The simulator cannot expose this class at all
findings.evidence: bridge/src/sim_frame.rs:45 SIM_MAX_ADU = 65535 and bridge/src/api/devices/simulation.rs:72 reports max_adu 65535. The sim is always a 16-bit right-and-left-identical container.
findings.consequence: Pass-making direction: every sim frame lands on the one ceiling the hardcoded constant happens to be right for.

findings.claim: The >90%-clipped reporting rule made a ruined frame silent
findings.evidence: Check 4 only warned above max_saturation_percent (0.90). A frame with 50% of pixels at the ceiling produced no error and no warning.
findings.consequence: Added a second tier at warn_saturation_percent (0.05). Kept as a WARNING, not an error: errors abort the exposure in bridge/src/unified_device_ops.rs, and a 5% tier promoted to error would abort runs on bright flats and moonlit fields.

changes: saturation_threshold_for_full_scale(full_scale) -> Option<u16>: threshold = ceiling - (ceiling >> 7), i.e. ~0.8% of headroom. Reproduces the historical constant exactly for 16-bit (65535 - 511 = 65024) and scales to 4095 -> 4064, 16383 -> 16256. Returns None below MIN_TRUSTED_FULL_SCALE (255) so a driver reporting a nonsense ceiling cannot drag the threshold under the sky background and fail every frame of the night.
ImageValidationOptions::sensor_max_adu: Option<u32> (+ ImageValidationOptions::for_sensor(max_adu)) — the declared container full scale, which takes precedence.

A declared ceiling the frame itself EXCEEDS is discarded: that is the documented bit_depth-vs-max_adu confusion (a driver advertising 4095 while its samples reach 65504), and honouring it would call a well-exposed frame completely saturated.

infer_full_scale_from_frame(): last-resort recovery of the container ceiling from the frame, used when the caller cannot supply max_adu (which is every production caller today). Only claims a ceiling when the peak lands exactly on 1023/4095/16383 AND at least max(16, total/2048) pixels pile up there, so a 16-bit frame whose brightest star happens to read 4095 is untouched.
Statistics pass now tracks count_at_max instead of counting saturated pixels inline (the threshold is not knowable until the peak is), then counts saturation in a second pass.
Checks 1/4/5 and the basic validate_image() all use the resolved threshold; debug log now prints the threshold alongside the saturation percentage.
Check 4 tiered: >90% 'Excessive saturation' (unchanged) / >5% 'Heavy saturation: X% clipped at/above N'.
tests_added: test_saturation_threshold_tracks_the_sensor_ceiling — headroom is a proportion of full scale (>=1 ADU, <=0.9%, >=0.6% for >=10-bit) and 16-bit still yields exactly 65024
test_declared_ceiling_decides_saturation_not_the_pixel_values — SAME pixel buffer, half at 4095: clipped on for_sensor(4095), silent on for_sensor(65535)
test_declared_ceiling_below_the_data_is_distrusted — declared 4095 with a 65504 pixel present must not report saturation
test_right_justified_12bit_clip_is_saturation_not_a_dead_sensor — through validate_image_with_options (the capture path's exact call)
test_half_clipped_frame_is_reported — 50% clipped must be reported and must carry the fraction
test_normal_star_field_with_a_few_clipped_cores_is_clean — 0.01% clipped cores on a 12-bit frame must stay silent (anti-false-alarm guard)

revert_check.method: Backed up the file, severed only the production wiring (ceiling resolution in validate_image_comprehensive, the lower saturation tier, and the resolved threshold in validate_image), left all tests intact, ran the suite, restored.
revert_check.severed_result: test result: FAILED. 60 passed; 5 failed — test_right_justified_12bit_clip..., test_right_justified_14bit_clip..., test_right_justified_clip_flagged_by_the_basic_validator_too, test_declared_ceiling_decides_saturation_not_the_pixel_values, test_half_clipped_frame_is_reported
revert_check.restored_result: cargo test --package skotiq_imaging: 484 passed; 0 failed (+12 integration, +1 doc)
revert_check.note: 3 of the 8 new tests pass in both states by design: the pure-helper proportion test and the two anti-false-positive guards.

verification: cd native/skotiq_native && cargo test --package skotiq_imaging -> 484 passed / 0 failed; cargo fmt -p skotiq_imaging --check clean; cargo clippy -p skotiq_imaging --all-targets clean
caveats: Production callers still pass no max_adu, so today the ceiling comes from the frame-evidence fallback. Threading the real value needs one line in a file owned by another agent: bridge/src/unified_device_ops.rs:732 should call skotiq_imaging::validate_image_comprehensive(&img_for_validation, ImageValidationOptions { expected_width: Some(w), expected_height: Some(h), is_bias_frame, ..ImageValidationOptions::for_sensor(<camera max_adu>) }) instead of validate_image_with_options. The camera's max_adu is available from CameraStatus (bridge/src/device.rs:128).

The frame-evidence fallback deliberately will not fire on a lightly clipped right-justified frame (fewer than ~0.05% of pixels at the ceiling). That is a miss by design — at that level nothing would be reported on a 16-bit sensor either — but it means a right-justified sensor's saturation percentage is under-counted until max_adu is threaded through.
No real right-justified camera was available to confirm on hardware; the delivery convention is taken from the INDI/ASCOM contract and from the SensorInfo doc comment in native/src/camera.rs.
